hypothesis: If a bird's egg is laid blunt end first, so that the sharp end comes out later, then in direct counts of oviposition the blunt end is the majority orientation.
pass_criterion: In Salamon and Kent 2014, every bird species with at least 20 eggs whose pointed-end-first and blunt-end-first counts are both stated has blunt-end-first share strictly above 0.5. If the domestic fowl is among those species, its blunt-end-first share is also strictly above 0.5. A share of exactly 0.5 is not a pass.
fail_criterion: Every such species has pointed-end-first share strictly above 0.5 (the sharp end comes out first). If at least one species with n>=20 is blunt-majority and at least one is pointed-majority, the verdict is mixed. If no species has at least 20 eggs with both counts stated, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable.
interpretation: The claim says the sharp end, where the egg was attached, comes out of the hen after the blunt end. That is read as blunt-end-first oviposition. 'The hen' names the domestic fowl; the scope is birds, especially the fowl, so other domestic birds in the same observation series count, and the fowl is reported separately when the paper gives a count for it. Cited percentages from earlier authors count only when this paper also states the numerator and denominator. The attachment-to-the-uterus clause is not separately measured.

test_contract.expected_observation: For each bird species with at least 20 observed layings, the number laid blunt end first exceeds the number laid pointed end first.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: For each such species, the number laid pointed end first exceeds the number laid blunt end first. Species that disagree with each other are a mixed result, not a pass.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A peer-reviewed series of direct oviposition observations that states pointed-end-first and blunt-end-first counts for bird eggs. Secondary citations count only with a numerator and a denominator printed in the source used here. Licence must allow retrieval of the publisher PDF.
test_contract.inference_method: Extract the printed counts, compute blunt/(blunt+pointed) per species, and apply the majority thresholds above. No model and no exclusion of double-yolked eggs unless the paper already separates them; single-yolked and unspecified layings are the primary rows, and double-yolked rows are reported but do not set the verdict.

datasets.name: Salamon and Kent 2014, Orientation of the egg at laying
datasets.license: Copyright Asian Network for Scientific Information 2014, as printed on the PDF; no Creative Commons grant is printed on the file
datasets.role: direct oviposition counts for geese and ducks, and cited hen fractions that print a numerator and a denominator

method: The publisher PDF was downloaded and rendered at 200 dpi with pdftoppm. Tesseract read each page. Domestic-goose blunt and total counts, the domestic-duck pointed-end-first fraction, and parenthetical hen fractions were taken from that text. Shares are blunt/(blunt+pointed). Fractions with n<20 are reported and do not enter the verdict. Hen series that each have n>=20 are pooled as domestic fowl. Double-yolked eggs have no paired counts in this paper.

measured.unit: eligible species (n>=20) with blunt-end-first share strictly above 0.5
measured.uncertainty: counts read by OCR from a scanned PDF; percentages recomputed from the extracted numerators

species.source_sentence: SY goose eggs: blunt-end-first count and total
124 of the 145 (85.52%) random layings were observed as pointed end first

excluded_below_n20.label: Bradfield 1951 as printed in this paper

caveats: The PDF is a scan, so the counts depend on OCR. Each percentage cited beside a fraction was recomputed from the extracted numerator and denominator.
Domestic fowl enters only through fractions this paper prints (Wood-Gush and Gilbert). Bradfield's 9 of 10 is below the pre-registered floor of 20 and is not in the verdict.
The attachment-to-the-uterus clause is not measured. Double-yolked eggs are discussed in the paper without a pointed-versus-blunt count, so they do not set the verdict.
